newsitem.title: USA: Rain to remain active across northern U.S. Midwest.
newsitem.headline: Rain to remain active across northern U.S. Midwest.

text.p: Rain and hail pounded portions of southern Minnesota early Thursday and more rain was forecast for the northern Midwest into early Friday, meteorologists said.
The rest of the Midwest was expected to stay hot and dry, they noted.
"They got blasted with a lot of severe weather, lot of hail and torrential rain," said Dave Taylor, Weather Services Corp meteorologist, of the Minneapolis area.
Minneapolis received about four inches of rain and surrounding areas 0.5 to two inches.
The rain storms should redevelop Thursday evening and extend from southern Minnesota and northern Iowa across northern Illinois and northern Indiana, said Taylor.

The remainder of the Midwest should remain dry through early next week, he said. Daytime highs in the mid 90s Fahrenheit will be replaced Sunday when a cool front should drop highs into the 80s through early next week.
Taylor said spotty showers may develop further south in the Midwest next week, but generally the area should be dry.
Freese-Notis Weather meteorologist Craig Solberg was more optimistic for rain in the dry areas of central Illinois next week, calling for "an excellent chance for rain" there.
"From today (Thursday) through Tuesday we are seeing almost daily chances of rainfall in that dry area," he said.
Sections of central Illinois have received about a tenth of the normal 30-day rainfall. But Solberg said normal rainfall was likely there next week.
Cooler weather should enter the Midwest Sunday, moving high temperatures down into the 80s from the 90-degree heat this week, he said.
